title: Change the particle's charge
hook: Change charge magnitude and predict circular-orbit radius.
misconception: circular-orbit radius doubles when charge magnitude doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply r = mv/(abs(q)B) to compare circular-orbit radius when charge magnitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a nonrelativistic particle at fixed mass and speed moving perpendicular to a fixed uniform magnetic field, r = mv/(abs(q)B). When charge magnitude doubles, circular-orbit radius becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model r = mv/(abs(q)B); scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a nonrelativistic particle at fixed mass and speed moving perpendicular to a fixed uniform magnetic field, with a nonzero initial result. If charge magnitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on circular-orbit radius?
recall.why: Apply r = mv/(abs(q)B) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
